struck: In a South Carolina condo, the cost of a repair beyond insurance and the reserve is a common expense, which every owner pays in the percentage set for the unit in the master deed.
use: In a South Carolina condo, every owner pays a share of the cost of keeping up and repairing the shared parts, in the percentage set for the unit in the master deed. After damage, what insurance and the reserve do not cover is shared the same way.

pattern: (at least|minimum( of)?|a minimum) 20 years|20 years of (projected|contributions|income)|20-year (plan|projection|outlook)
struck: At least 20 years of projected contributions, expenses and ending balances.
use: At least 30 years of projected income, expenses and ending balances.

struck: An HOA's budget is open to its members to inspect and copy.
use: HOA members can inspect and copy the budget and the accounting records after giving written notice five business days ahead.

struck: 70 percent or more is strong (special assessments are rare).
use: 70 percent or more is strong (a low risk of special assessments).

struck: The lender divides the yearly reserve line by the budgeted dues income, leaving out income for things like cable or internet, and special assessment income.
use: The lender divides the yearly reserve line by the budgeted dues income. It may leave out income for things like cable or internet, and special assessment income.

struck: Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac raise the test to 15 percent.
use: Freddie Mac raises the test to 15 percent; it says it made the change with its regulator and in alignment with Fannie Mae.

struck: A Florida condo budget must carry reserves for the roof, painting and paving, whatever their cost, and for any other item over $25,000.
use: A Florida condo budget must carry reserves for the roof, painting and paving, whatever their cost, and for any other item over $25,675 in 2026 (the line rises with inflation each year).

pattern: New Jersey[^.]{0,200}(every five years|at least every 5 years)
struck: A 2024 New Jersey law makes associations of planned developments do and pay for a capital reserve study to the national standard, reviewed at least every five years.
use: A 2024 New Jersey law makes associations of planned developments, condos among them, do and pay for a capital reserve study with a 30-year funding plan. For condo and co-op buildings with a concrete, masonry or steel frame, the study must be redone and reviewed at least every five years.

struck: Show the reserve balance and the study's recommendation in the budget, except as the condominium instruments provide.
use: Unless the condo's own papers say otherwise, the board must study reserves at least every five years and review them every year. When the study shows reserves are needed, the budget must show the cash saved and the study's recommendation.

struck: Our agents read a building's HOA documents for a buyer before the offer.
use: Our agents read the HOA documents for a buyer.
